_meta.indication: CRYSVITA is a fibroblast growth factor 23 (FGF23) blocking antibody indicated for the treatment of X-linked hypophosphatemia (XLH) in adult and pediatric patients 1 year of age and older.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study with a 24-week placebo-controlled treatment phase; CRYSVITA dosed 1 mg/kg every 4 weeks.
pivotal_trials.population: Adult XLH patients with serum phosphorus less than 2.5 mg/dL and skeletal pain at baseline.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of subjects achieving serum phosphorus above the lower limit of the normal range at the midpoint of the dose interval (2 weeks post dose).
pivotal_trials.result: 94% of CRYSVITA patients (64/68) achieved mean serum phosphorus above the LLN through week 24 vs 8% (5/66) of placebo; p < 0.0001.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=25%) in pediatric patients: headache (60%), injection site reaction (59%), vomiting (48%), pyrexia (48%), pain in extremity (42%), vitamin D decreased (32%). In adults (>=5% and >= 2 more than placebo): back pain (15% vs 9%), headache (13% vs 9%), tooth infection (13% vs 9%), restless legs syndrome (12% vs 8%), vitamin D decreased (12% vs 5%). Risks include hypersensitivity, hyperphosphatemia and injection site reactions.
target_moa: Burosumab is a human IgG1 monoclonal antibody that binds FGF23 and inhibits its interaction with the Klotho-FGF receptor complex, thereby countering FGF23-induced renal phosphate wasting and increasing serum phosphorus and 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D.

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because it did not raise significant public health questions on the role of the biologic.
